quests.instruction: Which of these does NOT need a hand wash straight afterward?
quests.hint: Look for the one where nothing messy or germy touches your hands.
quests.explanation: Hands pick up germs from animals, noses, and dirt. Looking at a book does not make hands dirty.
quests.funFact: Germs are too small to see without a microscope, so clean-looking hands may still need washing.

quests.instruction: What is the best way to cover a sneeze?
quests.hint: Choose the way that keeps germs off the things you touch.
quests.explanation: Sneezing into your elbow catches the germs without putting them on your hands. With a tissue, throw it away and then wash your hands.
quests.funFact: A sneeze can send tiny droplets surprisingly far across a room.

quests.instruction: A snack is ready at the park, but there is no sink nearby. What could a grown-up hand out first?
quests.hint: Think about something that cleans hands without water.
quests.explanation: Hand sanitizer can clean hands when there is no sink, and a grown-up should give it out and watch. Soap and water is still better when hands are really dirty.
quests.funFact: Sanitizer is for hands only and is never safe to swallow.

quests.instruction: Which is the correct order for washing hands?
quests.hint: Water has to come before soap can foam, and drying comes at the very end.
quests.explanation: Wetting hands helps soap foam, scrubbing loosens germs, rinsing washes them off, and drying finishes the job.
quests.funFact: Germs spread more easily from wet hands, so drying well matters too.

quests.instruction: After you add soap, how long should you scrub your hands?
quests.hint: Singing a short song twice can help you count.
quests.explanation: Twenty seconds gives soap time to loosen germs from your skin. A quick rub misses a lot.
quests.funFact: Singing the birthday song twice takes about 20 seconds.

quests.instruction: Which parts of your hands are easiest to miss when washing?
options: The flat part of your palms ✋
Every part of your hands equally 👋
quests.hint: Look for the tight spots where soap has trouble reaching.
quests.explanation: Spaces between fingers, thumbs, and under nails hide dirt. Scrub those on purpose.
quests.funFact: Keeping nails short makes it easier to keep them clean.

quests.instruction: How many times a day do dentists usually suggest brushing your teeth?
quests.hint: Ask yourself when your teeth have been busy for a long time.
quests.explanation: Brushing in the morning and at night removes the sticky film that builds up on teeth. Waiting until a tooth hurts is too late.
quests.funFact: Dentists also suggest regular check-ups, even when nothing hurts.

quests.instruction: After sticky, sugary sweets, what helps teeth the most?
quests.hint: Water can wash away what sugar leaves behind.
quests.explanation: Sugar sticks to teeth, and germs in the mouth turn it into acid. Rinsing with water washes some of it away until you can brush.
quests.funFact: Drinking water is one of the simplest habits for healthy teeth.

quests.instruction: Which snack is kindest to your teeth?
quests.hint: Which snack does not leave sugar clinging to teeth?
quests.explanation: Crunchy fruit is less sticky, and chewing makes saliva that rinses teeth. Sticky sweets and slowly sipped sugary drinks keep sugar on teeth for hours.
quests.funFact: Saliva is the mouth's own built-in cleaner.

quests.instruction: Who should check the bath water temperature before a young child gets in?
quests.hint: Hot water can burn skin fast, so someone experienced should decide.
quests.explanation: Hot water can burn a child's skin quickly. An adult tests the water before the child steps in.
quests.funFact: Many homes set their water heaters so tap water is not scalding.

quests.instruction: What is the safest way to get out of a wet bathtub?
quests.correctAnswer: Hold the side, step out slowly 🛁
options: Jump out as fast as you can 🤸
Hold the side, step out slowly 🛁
quests.hint: Wet feet and hard floors do not go well with speed.
quests.explanation: Wet surfaces are slippery, so slow, careful steps with a hand on the side help you stay upright.
quests.funFact: Towels placed beside the tub can soak up drips from your feet.

quests.instruction: Why should a young child never be left alone in the bath?
quests.correctAnswer: Even shallow water can be risky 💧
options: The water gets cold very fast 🧊
Even shallow water can be risky 💧
quests.hint: Think about what could happen if a little person slipped.
quests.explanation: A young child can slip under shallow water before anyone notices, so an adult stays close the whole time.
quests.funFact: Even a few centimeters of water can be dangerous for a toddler.

quests.instruction: Maya spreads her towel over the rail after a shower. Why is that better than leaving it in a heap?
quests.hint: Wet things dry when the air can touch them.
quests.explanation: Spread out, a towel dries quickly. A damp heap stays wet inside and starts to smell.
quests.funFact: Towels dry faster in a bathroom with an open window or a fan.

quests.instruction: A towel smells musty. What most likely went wrong?
options: It was hung up too high 📏
quests.hint: Smelly germs and mildew love damp places.
quests.explanation: Damp towels let mildew grow, and that causes the musty smell. Hang towels to dry and wash them regularly.
quests.funFact: A towel left damp in a ball can start to smell in about a day.

quests.instruction: Which cloth should you use to dry your face after washing?
quests.hint: The cloth should be clean, and made for people, not dishes.
quests.explanation: A clean personal towel keeps dirt and germs off your face. Dish towels and floor towels do other jobs.
quests.funFact: Giving each person a different color of towel avoids any mix-up.

quests.instruction: After flushing the toilet, which step comes next?
quests.hint: Germs travel on hands, so your hands need attention.
quests.explanation: Washing with soap removes germs picked up in the bathroom. It is one of the best ways to stay healthy.
quests.funFact: Many public bathrooms put up posters showing hand-washing steps, because everyone needs a reminder.

quests.instruction: Why do we flush the toilet?
quests.hint: Work out where the waste goes.
quests.explanation: Flushing sends waste away through pipes, so the bathroom stays clean and healthy.
quests.funFact: Some toilets have two flush buttons, a small one and a big one, to use less water.

quests.instruction: Besides waste, what is the only thing that belongs in a toilet?
quests.hint: Even wipes labeled flushable can clog pipes.
quests.explanation: Only toilet paper breaks apart in water. Toys and wipes can block the pipes, and then a plumber has to fix them.
quests.funFact: A blocked pipe can make a toilet overflow, which is why only paper goes in.

quests.instruction: Which job is done at the bathroom sink?
quests.hint: Think about jobs that use running water for your own body.
quests.explanation: The bathroom sink is for personal cleaning. Cooking and dishes belong in the kitchen.
quests.funFact: Many bathroom sinks have a small overflow hole near the top that stops water spilling over the edge.

quests.instruction: Which sink is better for rinsing dirty plates?
options: Either one is just the same 🤷
quests.hint: Food and personal cleaning should not share a sink.
quests.explanation: Food belongs in the kitchen, and the bathroom sink is for personal care. Keeping the two apart keeps both clean.
quests.funFact: Kitchen sinks are usually deeper so that pots and plates fit.

quests.instruction: Which habit keeps a bathroom sink hygienic?
quests.hint: Leftover residue sticks around and grows germs.
quests.explanation: A quick rinse leaves the sink free of toothpaste and soap scum. Residue makes it dirty, and food does not belong in the bathroom.
quests.funFact: A quick rinse of the sink takes about five seconds.

quests.instruction: What are germs?
quests.correctAnswer: Tiny living things you cannot see 🦠
options: Tiny living things you cannot see 🦠
Tiny soap bubbles in a sink 🫧
quests.hint: You would need a microscope to see them.
quests.explanation: Germs are microscopic living things, and some can make us sick. Washing and cleaning keep them from spreading.
quests.funFact: Not all germs are harmful. Many live on and in our bodies without causing problems.

quests.instruction: Which of these passes germs on most easily?
quests.hint: Work out what touches your mouth.
quests.explanation: A cup that has touched one mouth can pass germs to the next. Washing and drying help get rid of them.
quests.funFact: Germs travel on coughs, shared things, and unwashed hands.

quests.instruction: Sofia has a cold. What helps keep her family healthy?
quests.hint: The goal is to stop germs from traveling.
quests.explanation: Covering coughs and washing hands stops germs from reaching other people. Sharing cups or lots of hugs passes them on.
quests.funFact: Resting at home helps the body fight a cold.

quests.instruction: Why is a non-slip mat useful in a bathtub or shower?
quests.hint: Wet tubs can be very slippery.
quests.explanation: A non-slip mat grips both the tub and your feet, so you are less likely to fall.
quests.funFact: Many mats have small suction cups on the underside.

quests.instruction: Which of these must never go near bathtub water?
quests.hint: Think about which one needs electricity.
quests.explanation: Water and electricity are a dangerous mix, so plugged-in things stay far from baths and sinks. Plastic cups and toys are safe.
quests.funFact: Bathroom sockets are often placed away from the tub for this reason.

quests.instruction: A sibling is splashing so much that water is spreading over the floor. What is a good thing to suggest?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep the water in the tub 🛁
options: Keep the water in the tub 🛁
quests.hint: Wet floors make slipping likely.
quests.explanation: Water on a hard floor is slippery. Keeping the splashes in the tub helps everyone stay on their feet.
quests.funFact: A towel on the floor beside the tub soaks up drips.

quests.instruction: Luca comes home from a muddy football game. What should he do before sitting on the sofa?
options: Wipe his hands on the sofa 🛋️
quests.hint: Mud that touches the sofa stays there.
quests.explanation: Washing and changing keeps mud and germs off furniture. Wiping on the sofa spreads dirt around.
quests.funFact: Sports clubs often have showers so players can clean up before going home.

quests.instruction: Which set of things belongs in a personal hygiene kit?
quests.hint: A hygiene kit is for caring for your own body.
quests.explanation: Soap, a toothbrush, and a comb are for personal care. A sponge, bucket, and broom are for cleaning the home.
quests.funFact: Travel kits hold small bottles so you can keep clean away from home.

quests.instruction: Which morning bathroom routine takes care of the most hygiene needs?
options: Comb hair and skip the rest 💇
quests.hint: Count how many body-care jobs each choice includes.
quests.explanation: The first routine covers the toilet, hands, and teeth. The others cover only one job.
quests.funFact: Short routines done every day matter more than long ones done rarely.
